video_goal: Visually guide the user through flashing an SD card and physically connecting the components to boot up a Raspberry Pi 4.
required_subjects_and_props: Raspberry Pi 4 Model B board, MicroSD card, SD card reader, laptop, Raspberry Pi Imager software, micro-HDMI cable, USB keyboard/mouse, USB-C power supply, monitor

outline_steps.visual_action: Hands place a green Raspberry Pi 4 board, a MicroSD card, and a black USB-C power supply side-by-side on a clean wooden desk.
Fingers slide the MicroSD card into a USB SD card reader, then push the reader into the USB port of a laptop.
On the laptop screen, the mouse cursor clicks the white 'CHOOSE OS' button within the pink and white Raspberry Pi Imager UI.
The mouse cursor scrolls down the pop-up list and clicks on the 'Raspberry Pi OS (32-bit)' option.
The cursor clicks 'CHOOSE STORAGE', selects the mounted SD card drive, and then clicks the 'WRITE' button, showing a progress bar filling up.
Fingers pull the USB SD card reader out of the laptop and extract the MicroSD card from the reader.
Hands flip the Raspberry Pi 4 board upside down and slide the MicroSD card into the metal slot on the bottom edge until it is flush.
Hands plug a micro-HDMI cable into the first small port labeled 'HDMI0' located next to the USB-C port on the board.
Hands plug a USB mouse cable and a USB keyboard cable into the two silver USB 2.0 ports on the edge of the board.
Fingers push the USB-C power cable firmly into the USB-C port on the corner of the Raspberry Pi 4 board.
A solid red LED and a rapidly blinking green LED illuminate on the corner of the green circuit board.
The connected monitor transitions from black to the Raspberry Pi OS desktop, displaying a sunset wallpaper and a 'Welcome to Raspberry Pi' dialog box.
